item.title: Nepal Rasuwa Flood Situation Report No. 6
item.description:
Country: Nepal
Sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, UN Resident Coordinator in Nepal

Please refer to the attached file.

SITUATION OVERVIEW

More than a week after the 26 August flood, search and rescue has largely given way to relief operations. NDRRMA reports 1,259 deaths, 5,083 people out of contact and 12,038 rescued. Access remains the principal constraint, with damaged roads and bridges slowing the movement of relief supplies into upper Rasuwa, and several locations reachable only on foot.

Alongside the Government of Nepal, the Humanitarian Country Team launched a Flash Appeal in support of the Government-led response. The appeal seeks US$49.6 million to provide life-saving assistance to 84,270 people (19,284 households) in 17 municipalities across six districts: Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha and Tanahu. All identified affected people are targeted, of whom nearly 40 per cent are children.

Requirements cover ten sectors through the end of 2026, with roughly three quarters concentrated in five: food security (US$7.94 million), WASH (US$7.9 million), health (US$7.6 million), logistics and emergency telecommunications (US$7.33 million) and shelter (US$7.1 million). The appeal complements the Government's Official Disaster Relief Appeal of 27 August and the NDRRMA-led operation. It is a time-bound humanitarian response, not a recovery plan; recovery and reconstruction needs will be addressed through the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment.

To sustain the immediate response ahead of the appeal, the CERF allocation has been recalibrated to US$2.5 million, prioritizing life-saving assistance in the worst-affected districts.

The Logistics Cluster has been activated to support partners with logistics coordination, information management and common services, working with the Ministry of Home Affairs to identify and address transport bottlenecks. With WFP's support, a coordination base for the UN and partners is being established in Bidur, Nuwakot, providing shared operational and office space for agencies and cluster coordinators working closer to affected communities.

HUMANITARIAN NEEDS AND RESPONSE

Food and non-food items are in sufficient supply in the market areas in Bidur - Nuwakot. Relief supplies continue to build up in Nuwakot, as access challenges hinder the delivery of assistance to many of the most severely affected communities in Rasuwa.

Protection remains a key concern, as women, men, and children continue to share common spaces in displacement centres, raising potential protection risks and limiting privacy for vulnerable groups. Psychological counselling and social and behaviour change (SBC) interventions on personal and menstrual hygiene are needed.
Additional priorities include addressing WASH needs, improving displacement site management and tracking, establishing safe spaces for children, and providing specialized nutritious food to pregnant and breastfeeding mothers and children under five.

item.title: Nepal: Rasuwa Flood Situation Report No-6 (As of 5 September 2026)
item.description:
Country: Nepal
Sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, UN Resident Coordinator in Nepal

Please refer to the attached file.

  • So far, reports indicate that the Rasuwa floods have claimed 1,259 lives, with 5,083 people still out of contact and 12,038 rescued (NDRRMA, 3 September, 19:00).
  • 3,844 displaced people are living in 34 displacement sites in Nuwakot, Rasuwa, Dhading, and Kathmandu. IOM is supporting the Government’s response through the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) and estimates 4,288 households were affected by the floods, of which 2,886 households were displaced.
  • Access continues to be a constraint, with road blockages limiting the transportation of relief supplies to affected communities.
  • Activated on 27 April, the Global Logistics Cluster in Nepal is supporting humanitarian partners through coordination, information management, GIS mapping, and work with the Ministry of Home Affairs to prevent logistics bottlenecks.

item.title: Sudan Protection Cluster Alert: Blue Nile - Escalating Hostilities and Humanitarian Access Constraints
item.description:
Country: Sudan
Source: Protection Cluster

Please refer to the attached file.

Escalating hostilities in Blue Nile are driving new displacement, increasing protection risks and further constraining humanitarian access. More than 23,000 people have reportedly been displaced from Geissan and Al Kurmuk localities since 11 August 2026, while insecurity and movement restrictions are disrupting humanitarian operations and access to essential services.

The Protection Cluster is concerned that continued hostilities, possible further population movements, explosive ordnance contamination, seasonal flooding and existing pressure on services could further heighten risks for displaced people, refugees and host communities, particularly women, children, older people and persons with specific needs.

The alert reiterates its call on all parties to the conflict to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, facilitate safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access and civilian movement, and respect their obligations under International Humanitarian Law. It also calls on humanitarian actors and humanitarian leadership to sustain critical services, strengthen protection monitoring and preparedness, and maintain contingency arrangements for any further deterioration in the security and access environment.

item.title: Yemen: Flash Update: Escalation of hostilities and mass displacement in Maqbanah and Jabal Habashi districts, Ta'iz governorate (As of 4 September)
item.description:
Country: Yemen
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

  • Hostilities escalated along the Ta'iz frontlines in the early hours of Thursday, 3 September, with intense shelling and clashes in Maqbanah and Jabal Habashi districts.
  • An estimated 1,790 households have been displaced since 3 September, with movements continuing at the time of reporting.
  • Most displaced families are moving within Maqbanah and Jabal Habashi; others are arriving in Al Ma'afer, Ash Shamayatayn, Mawza and Dubab. Entire IDP sites, including Al-Hajab, Al-Rajehi and Hajjat Gabeh, have reportedly emptied, generating large-scale secondary displacement.
  • Ongoing shelling is restricting the ability of families to move to safer areas, and some households remain stranded in frontline locations.
  • Telecommunications disruptions are hampering information collection, verification and coordination, and emergency stocks are severely depleted, particularly Shelter/NFI and food assistance.

item.title: El Salvador: Latinoamérica y El Caribe Resumen de Situación Semanal al 4 de septiembre 2026
item.description:
Countries: El Salvador, Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached Infographic.

CIFRAS CLAVE

  • 91K hogares del Corredor Seco enfrentan pérdida de cosechas e ingresos por sequía
  • 123K personas asistidas por la ONU y sus socios en Colombia tras el terremoto de agosto 2026
  • 702 familias desplazadas asistidas tras violencia armada en Kenscoff, Haití

CENTROAMÉRICA: SEQUÍA

Una evaluación de Oxfam y Acción contra el Hambre realizada en julio y agosto detectó más de 91.000 hogares del Corredor Seco con pérdida de cosechas, ingresos y agua. Casi todos los hogares productores de maíz perdieron la cosecha de Primera 2026, con pérdidas casi totales en el oriente de El Salvador y Guatemala y el sur de Honduras. Dos tercios conservan reservas de maíz para tres semanas o menos, y los precios aumentaron 67% en Honduras y 32% en El Salvador respecto al año anterior. El Salvador informó que agosto fue el más seco desde 1971, tras la alerta roja del 25 de agosto por El Niño. OCHA coordina proyectos de Acción Anticipatoria en el Corredor Seco financiados por CERF, el Fondo Global de Emergencia de la ONU, mientras que el Fondo Humanitario Regional para América Latina y el Caribe (RHPF LAC) también apoya respuesta en el Corredor Seco.

ECUADOR: EL NIÑO

El organismo de monitoreo oceánico-atmosférico de Ecuador confirmó el 28 de agosto que El Niño cumplió los criterios técnicos de presencia oficial, con temperaturas del mar hasta 4 °C sobre el promedio y niveles del mar elevados. El Centro de Predicción Climática de la NOAA prevé que se fortalezca hasta finales de 2026. Los impactos varían: la costa registra inundaciones aisladas y la sierra enfrenta sequía y riesgo de incendios forestales. La Secretaría Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos (SNGR) declaró alerta roja nacional el 29 de agosto, designación que no equivale a un estado de emergencia pero ordena a los Comités de Operaciones de Emergencia provinciales y cantonales activar planes de preparación y respuesta, incluidas evacuaciones preventivas, movilización de recursos y protección para comunidades en riesgo de inundaciones, deslizamientos e incendios forestales.

COLOMBIA: TERREMOTO

Colombia reporta 466.606 personas afectadas por el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 del 10 de agosto en 16 departamentos, frente a 282.709 el 21 de agosto, incluidas 331 muertes, 4.519 heridos y 136 desaparecidos. Unas 73.378 viviendas son inhabitables y los daños en 4.287 escuelas afectaron a más de un millón de estudiantes. Chocó enfrenta además enfrentamientos armados y explosivos lanzados con drones que desplazaron a 912 personas de la zona rural de Sipí, mientras lluvias y deslizamientos afectaron a 2.814 hogares en Quibdó, la capital departamental. Los aportes internacionales superan los US$40 millones y 29 organizaciones han asistido a 123.000 personas en 49 municipios. Una evaluación del PNUD con la UNGRD, entidad nacional de gestión del riesgo de desastres, estima unos US$13.400 millones en daños directos, cerca de 2,3% del PIB.

HAITÍ: DESPLAZAMIENTO

Los socios humanitarios ampliaron la respuesta multisectorial en Kenscoff, comuna en las alturas de Puerto Príncipe, y al 2 de septiembre asistieron a 702 hogares desplazados con albergue y artículos no alimentarios. Clínicas móviles operaron en Lotin, Thomassin 25 y Kenscoff, y el PMA iniciará la asistencia alimentaria la semana del 6 de septiembre. La respuesta sigue al ataque de grupos armados de la noche del 23 de agosto, que dejó al menos 47 muertos y 22 heridos, incluidas más de 20 personas ejecutadas dentro de una iglesia donde se habían refugiado. Los atacantes quemaron viviendas y secuestraron a 50 personas; seis niños y siete mujeres fueron liberados. La OIM reporta 4.238 personas desplazadas, 80% en familias de acogida. Violencia similar desplazó a cerca de 6.000 personas de Kenscoff en julio.
